title: Polychrome Sequence Viewer: multi-track request lens for tracing and cost correlation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design a compact, scalable request drill-down called the Polychrome Sequence Viewer (PSV). PSV is a horizontally-scrollable, multi-track timeline that layers span groups, service lanes, and a continuous cost heattrack derived from inference token billing. The goal is a single-pane experience for on-call and SRE workflows: find noisy spans, pivot on correlation IDs, compare model variant runs, and surface cost spikes aligned to trace time. This ticket covers low-fidelity exploration, an interactive Figma prototype for stakeholder review, and a developer handoff spec for perf-sensitive rendering techniques.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates lane collapse/expand, span grouping, and a scrubber synchronized with span details panel
Cost heattrack overlay shows per-second cost density and links to token-level breakdowns in the Console Cost view
Filter rail supports correlation ID quick jump, service name, model-variant tags, and span-status (error/warn/info)
Performance plan documented for traces up to 50k spans: virtualization strategy, progressive loading, and server-side aggregation
Design tokens and accessible color palette defined (WCAG AA contrast for primary lane colors)
engineering_notes: Backend: trace-aggregator-v2 must expose a /traces/:id/summary endpoint that returns lane buckets and aggregated cost per timeslice
Rendering: use windowed virtualization for span lanes, collapse long idle segments into 'gap' markers with expand on demand
Sampling: UI will indicate when trace is sampled; for sampled traces provide link to full-raw trace in infra for forensic workflows
KV cache events and batch boundaries should be represented as small inline markers to help correlate cache hits with latency drops
Pagination: implement progressive loading for extremely long traces with a 2s interactive loading budget for first paint
decisions: Color strategy: polychrome palette by service with desaturated background lanes to preserve contrast for overlays
Cost overlay: continuous gradient heattrack aligned to timeline instead of per-span badges to reduce visual clutter
Span grouping: default by request-phase (parse, route, model-call, postprocess) with user override to group by service
Virtualization: client windowing + server-side aggregation at >5000 spans to keep memory under 150MB
Correlation search: users can paste correlation ID and PSV will center and flash the matched span(s)
review_feedback: PM (Janelle Morris): prioritize fast center-on-correlation-ID flows and confirm links to the Cost Explorer
Eng (Ravi Gupta): prefer lightweight SVG lane rendering initially; canvas fallback later for extreme traces
SRE (Liam O'Connor): add visual indicators for retries and network-level retries for easier incident TTR
Accessibility (Tina Huang): ensure keyboard scrubbing and focusable span rows; provide a high-contrast theme
